transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I’m here because things at work have been getting strange, not strange like the customers—though some of them do buy the same gum every day, which I notice—but me, I guess. I’m a cashier, and I keep getting stuck at the register doing things that don’t really fit what’s happening. Like I’ll tap the scanner in a pattern, or I’ll just freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while the person is standing there waiting.

Last week I got written up for it, and that’s… that’s why I figured I should come in.
How are these experiences at work affecting you emotionally?

Emotionally… I don’t know, it’s kind of flat, I guess. I mean, I still care about my wife and the kids, that hasn’t gone away. But I don’t have much push to do things I used to just do, like call my son at college or go meet the kayak group. I keep meaning to fix this little lamp in the garage too—simple wiring thing, probably ten minutes if I actually start—but it just sits there.

And when people ask me what’s wrong, I mostly just shrug. It’s not that I’m trying to be rude. I just… can’t find much to say.
Do you find yourself repeating these patterns, like tapping the scanner, because you feel like you have to, or is it more that you just get stuck doing them?

More like I get stuck, I think. It’s not like I’m thinking, “I have to tap it or something bad happens.” I’ll just be at the register and my hand starts doing the scanner thing—tap, tap, tap in this little pattern—or I’ll stop with my hand over the cash drawer, and the customer is just there looking at me.

It doesn’t fit the moment, you know? Like I know I’m supposed to be making change or scanning the next item, but I’m caught in it. That’s what got me written up last week. Well, that and the manager was already irritated about the coupon drawer being messy, which wasn’t really my fault, but… yeah, it’s more getting stuck than feeling forced.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind?

I’m not sure… I mean, thoughts repeat in the normal way, I guess. Like I’ll keep thinking about whether I locked the car, or if my manager is going to bring up the write-up again, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.

Sometimes a song gets stuck in my head, but that happens to everybody, right? My wife had that one commercial jingle in her head for three days once—drove her nuts. So… I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed one specific thought going around and around, not like the tapping thing.
Do you feel anxious when these patterns happen or when you're unable to do them?

Anxious… not exactly, no. It’s more embarrassing after I realize it’s happening. Like at the register, I’ll get stuck tapping the scanner in that little pattern, or I’ll just freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while someone’s standing there waiting, and then I sort of come back to it and think, “Why am I doing this?”

I mean, the customer doesn’t know what to do, and then the line gets backed up, and the manager—well, last week that’s what got me written up. Though he’s been on edge about other stuff too, like the coupon drawer, which is always a mess no matter who’s working. But no, it’s not panic if I can’t do it. It’s more like I get caught in it and then feel stupid afterward.
Do you ever feel like you have to perform specific rituals or behaviors outside of work?

Outside of work… I mean, not really rituals like that, no. It’s mostly at the register where I notice it, because everything’s moving fast and there’s a customer right there, and then I’m doing that scanner tapping thing or my hand just kind of stops over the cash drawer.

At home I might get sidetracked, but it’s not like I have a whole routine I have to do. The work thing is the problem. That’s why I came in, really—because it doesn’t fit what I’m supposed to be doing, and last week it got me written up. My manager made it sound like I was being careless, but I wasn’t trying to do it.
Have you noticed any changes in how you interact with your family or friends since these experiences at work started?

Yeah… I guess I have. I mean, I don’t know if it’s because of work exactly, but since all this started getting noticed there, I’ve kind of pulled back.

I’m on a formal warning now, so when I get home I keep thinking about that, and then I don’t call people back. My sister will leave a message and I’ll mean to call, and then it’s two days later. Same with friends—we used to talk about going kayaking, there’s this place we like that has a decent launch if the water isn’t too low, but I haven’t been following through with plans.

It’s not like I’m mad at anybody. I just… I’m not keeping up the way I used to.
Do you feel like you have to do specific things in a certain way when you're not at work?

Not really… I mean, I don’t think so. At home I do things my own way, sure, like everybody does. I put the mail on the little table by the door, and then sometimes it piles up because half of it is flyers for roofing companies, which is funny because I don’t even own the place—

But no, I don’t feel like I have to do things in some exact way when I’m not at work. I haven’t noticed anything like the register stuff happening at home.
Do you have any thoughts that disturb you or keep coming back to you even when you try to think of something else?

I’m not sure… I mean, everybody has things that go around in their head, right? Like if I’m worried about work, I’ll think about that warning or whether I’m going to mess up at the register again.

But I don’t know if I’d call it disturbing thoughts exactly. Sometimes I try to watch TV and then I’m still thinking about some little thing, like whether I paid the electric bill, and then I remember the envelope is probably under those grocery flyers by the door—those ads come every week, it’s ridiculous.

So… I guess I haven’t noticed a particular thought that keeps forcing its way in, if that’s what you mean. More just regular worrying, I think.
Do you feel upset or uncomfortable when you're unable to do the tapping pattern or other repetitive things you mentioned?

Yeah… uncomfortable, I guess, but not like if I don’t do it something terrible will happen. It’s more like I get stuck.

At the register, I’ll start tapping the scanner in this pattern, and it doesn’t really fit what’s going on because the customer is just standing there waiting. Or I’ll have my hand over the cash drawer and just freeze for a second too long. The drawer makes that little clunk sound when it opens—actually ours sticks sometimes, especially the left one—but anyway, I just sort of stop.

That’s what got me written up last week. Not because I was trying to be difficult. I just… I couldn’t move on fast enough.
Do you feel like you have to repeat any behaviors or actions when you're not at work?

Not really when I’m not at work, no… I mean, I’ll do normal things twice sometimes, like checking if the door’s locked, but I don’t think that’s what you mean.

The thing I came in about is more at the register. I get stuck doing things that don’t fit the moment, like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or I freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is just standing there. And then I’m aware of them waiting, which makes it worse somehow. That’s what got me written up last week.

At home, I don’t really have that same kind of repeating thing.
Do you feel like you have to perform any specific actions or behaviors at home or outside of work to relieve anxiety or discomfort?

I don’t think so… not in a specific way. Like at home I might straighten something if it’s crooked, or I’ll move the mail off the chair because I hate when it piles up there—my brother used to leave newspapers everywhere, drove me crazy—but I’m not doing it to make anxiety go away exactly.

Outside work, I can’t think of a thing I have to do. It’s mostly just… I don’t know, regular habits. The stuff that feels like I get stuck seems to happen at the register more than anywhere else.
Do you feel like these patterns of behavior, such as tapping the scanner, are affecting your relationships with others or your overall well-being?

Yeah, I guess it is affecting things. At work especially. I’m on a formal warning now, which… I mean, they call it “formal,” like it’s a school detention or something, but it’s my job, so it feels worse than that.

And outside of shifts, I don’t know, I’ve kind of stopped keeping up with people. Friends will text about kayaking—there’s this place we used to go, not too far, the water gets really flat in the morning—and I just don’t answer, or I say maybe and then don’t go. Family calls too. I used to be better about calling back. Now I let it sit. So yeah… overall, I’m not really doing as well with people as I used to.
Do you feel like these behaviors are significantly interfering with your ability to function at work or in your personal life?

Yeah… I think it is. I mean, at work it’s pretty obvious now because I’m on that formal warning, and once something’s in writing it’s hard to pretend it’s nothing.

And then outside work… I don’t know, I used to be better about people. Friends still ask about kayaking sometimes—there’s this one lake where you have to get there early before the wind picks up—and I keep meaning to answer, but then I just don’t. Same with family calls. I let them sit, and then it’s been too long, and then I feel awkward calling back. So yeah, it’s interfering more than I want to admit.
Do you feel compelled to perform any specific rituals or behaviors when you are alone at home?

When I’m alone at home? Not really… I mean, I do normal home stuff, like I’ll pick up cups or straighten the TV remote if it’s sitting weird, but I don’t think of it like a ritual.

Sometimes I’ll start sorting through mail and then somehow I’m thinking about the grocery store flyers, which reminds me of how prices keep going up, and then I’m annoyed for twenty minutes… but that’s not like I have to do it a certain number of times or anything. I haven’t really noticed anything like that at home.
Do you feel upset if you are interrupted or unable to complete one of these repetitive patterns, like the scanner tapping?

Yeah… I mean, upset maybe isn’t the exact word, but I get kind of stuck there. Like at the register, if I’m doing that tapping thing on the scanner and then someone says something, or the line moves, it’s like my hand doesn’t catch up with the moment.

Or I’ll freeze with my hand over the cash drawer, which is embarrassing because the customer’s just standing there, and people get impatient. I used to be pretty quick at that part—cash, receipt, bag, next person—but lately it’s like the whole rhythm gets jammed. Last week that’s part of what got me written up, I think. They didn’t say it exactly like that, but… yeah, it’s not good.
Do you feel distressed when you're not able to do the tapping pattern or other repetitive things you mentioned?

Yeah, I do get distressed, I guess… mostly because it throws everything off. It’s not like I’m thinking, “I must finish this,” exactly, but when I can’t do the tapping pattern, or when I get interrupted, I sort of lock up.

Like at the register, I’ll be tapping the scanner in that pattern, and then suddenly the customer’s waiting and I’m just standing there with my hand over the cash drawer. It doesn’t fit the moment, you know? And then I notice them looking at me, and that makes it worse.

That’s kind of why I came in. Last week it got bad enough that I got written up at work, and once work puts something like that on paper… I mean, I’ve worked registers a long time, you learn people’s little habits, coupons, the way they stack their groceries—sorry, I’m getting off track. But yeah, it bothers me because I’m getting stuck when I’m supposed to just keep things moving.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind even when you try to focus on something else?

I’m not sure… I don’t think I have a thought like that, like one sentence repeating over and over. Sometimes my mind keeps circling around something, like work or money or something somebody said, but I think everybody does that, right?

I’ll try to focus and then I’m thinking about the store schedule, and then that reminds me of the manager’s handwriting on the board—he writes the sevens funny—and then I’m thinking about my old math teacher for some reason. So it wanders, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean by repeating thoughts.
Do you feel like these patterns of behavior are aimed at preventing some dreaded event or situation?

No… I don’t think it’s like I’m trying to stop something bad from happening, not like that.

It’s more that I get caught in it. Like at the register, I’ll be tapping the scanner in a pattern, or I’ll just freeze with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is waiting, and it doesn’t match what I’m supposed to be doing. The line is there, people are watching, and I know I should move on.

That’s actually why I came in, because last week it got bad enough I got written up at work. I’ve done cashier stuff a long time, so it’s embarrassing when I’m just… stuck like that.
Do you think your behaviors are aimed at reducing anxiety or discomfort?

I don’t know if I’d say I’m doing it to reduce anxiety, exactly. It’s more like I get caught in it before I’ve even thought about why.

Like at the register, I’ll start tapping the scanner in a pattern, or I’ll just sort of stop with my hand over the cash drawer, and the customer’s waiting there. And then I realize, you know, this doesn’t fit what’s happening. I’m supposed to be moving the line along, not standing there like that.

I guess it does get uncomfortable once I notice people looking. Last week it got bad enough that I got written up, which is really why I came in. I’ve worked registers for years, and usually I can keep things moving, but lately I keep getting stuck.

Sometimes I’ll start sorting through mail and then somehow I’m thinking about the grocery store flyers, which reminds me of how prices keep going up, and then I’m annoyed for twenty minutes… but that’s not like I have to do it a certain number of times or anything. I haven’t really noticed anything like that at home.
